commenti.body: It's hard for me to seperate Chevy the asshole from Chevy the actor.  There were a couple bits in Community where he delivered pretty good stuff.  But most of the time I just feel like he's playing Chevy Chase.

like half of these scan as not real or very loosely "considered" to me. There's no fuckin way he was ever seriously considered for Han Solo lmao. So many actors auditioned for that part, and he was not among them.

I’ve never heard that either. I will say, now that I’ve heard it, I can picture him doing a decent job as Solo in the first film. Not Empire though unless he decided to really dedicate himself to improving his acting.

Star Wars? I'm having a hard time grasping why you'd think about casting TV comic Chevy Chase as Han Solo in 1977. "I'm Han Solo and you're not." Maybe Belushi as Vader? Hell, Belushi and Carrie Fisher were pals! And Bill Murray could sing the theme! *Hey kids this could work!*
laughing thinking about him saying "I know" in his normal smug Chevy cadence before he's lowered into the carbonite.

I think it's entirely possible. Star Wars would have been casting in 1975 just as he was first appearing on SNL.

So at that time he wouldn't have been an established actor with a cemented brand yet.

Can't say there's anything here that I would really want to see him swapped in to. Some of them would almost certainly be worse with him.

My heart hurts imagining him in Roger Rabbit.

I can see a lot of these movies being forgotten flops had he been cast. I mean, we know now that Kevin Spacey is a sleazebag, but Chase did not have the chops to pulled off Lester Burnham in American Beauty. I can't conceive of Paul Schrader seriously considering him for American Gigolo. I think Arthur would have tanked with him in the lead.

Disclaimer: I don’t particularly like Chevy Chase.

I’d love to see a sources for some of these, especially the one that proves he was considered for Indiana Jones. I find it highly unlikely Spielberg would have accepted Chevy for that role, not even on the short list.

To answer your question, none. He would have been fine in some of the mediocre films on your list, because he’s a mediocre actor. He shined in his comedies because they were written for his style of comedy; underplayed absurdism, aloof characters who are oblivious to their aloofness, put into bizarre scenarios. He lacks the ability to provide earnestness to any of the serious roles on your list.
